subject: Embedding cost structure and commit options
messages:
From: Ariel Gomez <ariel.gomez@dataforge.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@dataforge.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Embedding pricing model questions and RFQ

Jonas — thanks for the demo yesterday. DataForge is evaluating a migration from our in-house vector pipeline to a hosted embeddings provider. Before we move forward we'd like a clear picture of how Redwood prices embeddings and what options exist for enterprise customers. High level questions: 1) Is pricing strictly per-vector, or do you also offer per-token/byte models for higher-dimension vectors? 2) How do you handle dimensionality — do you charge different rates for 512 / 768 / 1536+ dims, or is there a multiplier? 3) We have a dataset of ~85M vectors (mostly 512d) and expect ~2M new vectors per month. What would an indicative monthly cost look like for hosted API usage (no dedicated pool at first)? 4) Do you support commitment tiers (12/24 months) with look-through discounts and overage rates? 5) Are there separate charges for embeddings generation vs storage/ingestion bandwidth? Please find our short RFQ attached. Looking for a ballpark quote to present to finance next week.

Appreciate a clear pricing table and any recommended packaging for predictable unit economics.

Thanks,
Ariel
Ariel Gomez
Head of Data Platforms, DataForge
A: +1 415 555 0113

---
Attachment: DataForge_RFP_Embeddings.xlsx (spreadsheet)

-------------------------
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Gomez <ariel.gomez@dataforge.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embedding pricing model questions and RFQ

Ariel — great questions and thanks for the RFQ. I pasted quick answers below and looped in Neha (pricing) and Rishi (solutions) so we can provide 2–3 packaging scenarios and an attached rate card. Short answers up front: 1) We price hosted embeddings primarily per-vector. We also publish a per-token equivalent for teams that intermix text/generation and embeddings to make apples-to-apples comparisons. 2) Dimensionality is handled via tiered per-vector rates (512d base, + multiplier bands for higher dims). 3) For 85M existing / 2M new vectors per month we can run a baseline hosted estimate; see scenarios Neha will send. 4) Yes — standard commitment tiers (monthly pay-as-you-go, 12m, 24m) with graduated discounts and fixed overage rates. 5) Embedding generation is billed at the time of inference (per-vector or per-token equivalent). Storage/hosting is an optional add-on (we can white-label S3/backing store pricing or you can keep your own storage if you prefer).

I'll defer to Neha for the numbers and Rishi for implementation notes (batching, deduping, dimensionality migration). We can schedule a short call Friday or early next week to walk DataForge finance through the scenarios.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

-------------------------
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, Ariel Gomez <ariel.gomez@dataforge.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Embedding pricing model questions and RFQ

Ariel / team — attaching a concise rate card and three packaging scenarios below. I tried to give clear line items so finance can model the options. Attachment: redwood_embedding_ratecard_v3.pdf (pdf) — includes unit economics, overage rules, and commit discounts. Please note these numbers are for hosted API only; Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) pricing is separate. Summary (hosted embeddings): - Baseline unit (512 dims): $0.00055 per vector (per inference call). This is our published list price for casual usage. - Dimension multipliers: 512d = base; 768d = base * 1.35; 1536d+ = base * 2.1. We can also support custom quantized model variants which reduce per-inference CPU/GPU time; those get an extra multiplier reduction on request. - Per-token equivalent: for teams combining completion + embedding usage, we publish $0.000006 / token as a reference (not a replacement for per-vector billing). Packaging scenarios (monthly expected ingress of 2M vectors; existing corpus 85M): Scenario A — Pay-as-you-go (no commit)  - Per-vector: $0.00055  - Estimated monthly generation cost (2M new vectors): $1,100  - No storage included; ingestion bandwidth billed separately if using Redwood-managed store Scenario B — 12-month 50k/month commit (mid-tier)  - Committed monthly spend: $50,000  - Effective per-vector after commit credit: ~$0.00032 (applies to all vectors generated under the commitment)  - Overage after commit billed at 1.6x the effective unit rate Scenario C — Enterprise reserved (recommended for predictable unit economics)  - 24-month commit: negotiable, example: $200k/month commit  - Committed unit below: ~$0.00020 per vector (512d)  - Includes 90-day SLO-backed throughput and optional storage add-on (custom pricing) Notes & clarifications: - Existing corpus ingestion (85M) can be one-time bulk ingestion; we can discount the migration ingestion by up to 50% depending on transfer method and timing (bulk migration promotion). - We do not charge for vector reads at query-time beyond inference cost if you use our hosted storage; nearest-neighbor search compute is billed separately under a retrieval SKU if you want a fully managed FAISS-like service. Search SKU example pricing is provided in the attached rate card. - Batches: we recommend batching at 512–1024 items to minimize per-vector overhead; Redwood Optimize can suggest batching parameters for your workload. - Model support: Redwood supports a catalog of embeddings models (open-source and Redwood-verified). For low-latency, high-throughput we recommend our 512d default; if you need semantic fidelity at 1536d we can provision the higher-dimension variant (different unit rates apply). Next steps: 1) I attached the rate card; please confirm which scenario you want modeled against your 85M corpus. 2) If you share a sample of your vector size distribution and expected QPS for retrievals we can provide a precise TCO including search SKU and storage. 3) If you want an internal PO/contract, I can draft a 12-month term sheet with explicit overage rules.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

---
Attachment: redwood_embedding_ratecard_v3.pdf (pdf)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Gomez <ariel.gomez@dataforge.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Embedding pricing model questions and RFQ

Ariel — quick implementation notes to go with Neha's scenarios: - If you plan to keep vectors in your own store and only use Redwood for generation, we can gate calls through your VPC (private deployment) but then storage is on you (no storage charge from Redwood). In that case we bill strictly for generation calls at the per-vector rate. - If you want Redwood-managed search (fully hosted retrieval), add the Search SKU. Example: for 2M vectors/month ingest and ~50k QPS read traffic across small-sized queries, expect a search SKU add-on in the order of $6k–$14k/month depending on replication and latency SLOs. - Migration: we can schedule a parallel ingestion window and support delta updates; tooling available to deduplicate and compress similar vectors before ingestion to minimize billing. - Model transitions: we can re-embed historic vectors into higher dims incrementally; that re-embedding is billed as generation work (but eligible for migration discounts as Neha noted).

Happy to schedule a 30-min technical readout next week to map the migration path.

-Rishi
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
